Description: Directs the program to the folder containing raw SnackerTracker data files
The date on which data recording began
The unit of time with which final outputs should be presented
Indicates whether raw data should be cropped to 24-hour timeframe(s)
If 24-hour cropping is applied, indicates how many 24-hour periods will be kept
Effect of Increasing: Increases total dataset duration in 24-hour blocks
Effect of Decreasing: Decreases total dataset duration in 24-hour blocks

Description: Also a descriptive variable. Defines when lights turn on
Effect of Increasing: Shifts light-regions later in time (to the right) relative to otherwise unfiltered mass recordings
Effect of Decreasing: Shifts light-regions earlier in time (to the left) relative to otherwise unfiltered mass recordings

Description: Also a descriptive variable. Defines when lights turn off
Effect of Increasing: Shifts dark-regions later in time (to the right) relative to otherwise unfiltered mass recordings
Effect of Decreasing: Shifts dark-regions earlier in time (to the left) relative to otherwise unfiltered mass recordings

Description: Also a descriptive variable. Defines the time at which recordings began
Effect of Increasing: Shifts data recordings to the right (later in time) relative to otherwise unaltered light-defined regions
Effect of Decreasing: Shifts data recordings to the left (earlier in time) relative to otherwise unaltered light-defined regions

Description: Indicates whether data collected when switch 1 has a status of 1 (on) should be cropped and interpolated
If switch 1 cropping is applied, crops and interpolates mass data where switch 1 = 1
If switch 1 cropping is applied, crops and interpolates light data where switch 1 = 1
If switch 1 cropping is applied, provides the option to invert switch values (i.e., 1 = 0 and 0 = 1)
Indicates whether data collected when switch 2 has a status of 1 (on) should be cropped and interpolated
If switch 2 cropping is applied, crops and interpolates mass data where switch 2 = 1
If switch 2 cropping is applied, crops and interpolates light data where switch 2 = 1
If switch 2 cropping is applied, provides the option to invert switch values (i.e., 1 = 0 and 0 = 1)
If applied, the user will be able to exclude a range of measurements from the start of recordings
If applied, the user will be able to exclude a range of measurements from the end of recordings
If any cropping is to be applied, this allows data retention to specifically begin when lights turn on or off
If light cropping is applied, this indicates whether data retention should begin when lights turn 'on' or 'off'
If 24-hour cropping is not applied, indicate the index of the first data point which should be retained
Enables users to shift and align 24-hour outputs to begin at light or dark onset
Specifies the number of indexed datapoints which are to be truncated from the start of recordings
Effect of Increasing: Retains less total data beginning later in time (i.e., removing more from the start of recordings)
Effect of Decreasing: Retains more total data beginning earlier in time (i.e., removing less from the start of recordings)

Description: Specifies the number of indexed datapoints which are to be truncated from the end of recordings
Effect of Increasing: Retains more total data by terminating recordings later in time (i.e., removing less from the end of recordings)
Effect of Decreasing: Retains less total data by terminating recordings earlier in time (i.e., removing more from the end of recordings)

Description: Determines the number of data points which should be incorporated into baseline establishment, which will be used as a start-buffer for data filtering
Effect of Increasing: Enables a longer filtering baseline and longer windows of band-pass filtering. Excessively high values may result in over-conservative filtering.
Effect of Decreasing: Shortens the filtering baseline and available windows for band-pass filtering. Values which are too low will not enable sufficient truncations upon band-pass filter application

Description: Removes datapoints which are greater or less than the prior value by the value herein specified
Effect of Increasing: Results in a less-restrictive filter (removes fewer datapoints)
Effect of Decreasing: Results in an increasingly-restrictive filter (removes more datapoints)

Description: The span over which measurement values will be checked for whether they fall within the band-pass filter
Effect of Increasing: Results in a more-restrictive filter which applies band-pass criteria over a greater range of indexed datapoints
Effect of Decreasing: Results in a less-restrictive filter which applies band-pass criteria across fewer indexed datapoints

Description: Defines the number of data points which can be incorporated into a moving-mean filter
Effect of Increasing: Increases preliminary data-smoothing. Data appears more clean, however important information may be lost
Effect of Decreasing: Decreases preliminary data-smoothing. Data appears less-clean, however more information from raw recordings is maintained

Description: Selects which mass filter combination should be applied to raw data and used for subsequent processing

Loops through the specified number of subsequent data points to check whether each corresponds to food being consumed (i.e., mass decreases and increases for filtered and flipped plots, respectively). Data points not meeting criteria (also defined by shiftTolerance) are set to the directly preceding value, and all following data are shifted accordingly
Effect of Increasing: Results in a more-restrictive filter as a greater number of subsequent data points can be identified as erraneous and shifted accordingly
Effect of Decreasing: Results in a less-restrictive filter as a fewer subsequent data points can be identified as erraneous and shifted

Description: Defines shift filter tolerance. shiftTolerance*100 represents the percentage of data points within a shiftFilter loop which must be less than the indexed value.
Effect of Increasing: The shift filter can be more readily applied; fewer 'outlier' values are required for shift correction
Effect of Decreasing: The shift filter is not as easily applied; fewer 'outlier' values are permitted

Description: Determines whether a chip filter will be applied. If the difference between a user-specified start and end value (chipStartTime and chipEndTime respectively) exceeds chipMass, all subsequent data will be shifted to the value directly preceeding chipStartTime
For each chip filter, the user must specify the mass cutoff which the difference between initial and final flanking values must exceed for application
Effect of Increasing: Results in a more-restrictive filter (i.e., a greater mass difference is required for filter application)
Effect of Decreasing: Results in a less-restrictive filter (i.e., the chip filter can be applied upon smaller mass differences)

Description: Defines the start-point defining the flanked region for chip filter application
Defines the end-point defining the flanked region for chip filter application
Enables additional chip filters

Variable Name: Shift, plateau, and chip filter selection
Description: Selects which shift, plateau, and chip filter combination should be applied to mass data and used for subsequent processing
Determines the number of data points across which the derivative of the cumulative food intake plot will be calculated
Effect of Increasing: Rates are calculated across a longer timeframe. Feeding patterns may be easier to visualise, however more detailed insights may be lost
Effect of Decreasing: Rates are calculated across a shorter timeframe. Feeding patterns may be more difficult to visualise (i.e., 'noisier'), however more detailed insights may be retained

Description: Determines the number of data points across which the derivative of the cumulative animal-device interactions plot will be calculated
Effect of Increasing: Rates are calculated across a longer timeframe. Patterns of animal-device interactions may be easier to visualise, however more detailed insights may be lost
Effect of Decreasing: Rates are calculated across a shorter timeframe. Patterns of animal-device interactions may be more difficult to visualise (i.e., 'noisier'), however more detailed insights may be retained

Description: If a sharp change in rates is flagged, the user is asked whether this may be due to error. If so, a mean smoothing filter is applied
Determines whether LDR filtering should be applied
If light filtering is to be applied, the user must indicate whether this should be continuous (i.e., smoothing) or binary (i.e., assigned by thresholding)
Effect of Increasing: N/A (0 for binary, or 1 for continuous)
Effect of Decreasing: N/A (0 for binary, or 1 for continuous)

Description: If binary light filtering is specified, the user can apply a first-round of smoothing before binarisation
If binary smoothing is to be applied, the user must define the window over which means will be calculated
Effect of Increasing: Increases preliminary data-smoothing. Data appears more clean, however important information may be lost
Effect of Decreasing: Decreases the amount of preliminary data-smoothing. Data appears less-clean, however more information from raw recordings is maintained

Description: For binary light filtering, this specifies the threshold wherein greater values = 1 and lesser-values = 0
Effect of Increasing: Brighter lighting is needed to be represented by '1'. Results in a more strict filter.
Effect of Decreasing: Dimmer lighting is sufficient for representation by a '1'. Results in a less-strict filter.

Description: Apply data smoothing to continuous light measurements without subsequent binarisation
Effect of Increasing: Increases preliminary data-smoothing. Data appears more clean, however important information may be lost
Effect of Decreasing: Decreases the amount of preliminary data-smoothing. Data appears less-clean, however more information from raw recordings is maintained

Description: Enables the user to 'bin' and thus compress data
If file compression is to be applied, the user must indicate whether it should be applied as a factor of file or bin size
Effect of Increasing: N/A (0 for bin size, 1 as a factor)
Effect of Decreasing: N/A (0 for bin size, 1 as a factor)

Description: Defines binned timeframes
Effect of Increasing: Outputs arrays are smaller in size and easier to handle for subsequent processing. However, increasing bin size may conceal data insights
Effect of Decreasing: Outputs arrays are larger in size however may be more difficult to handle during subsequent processing. However, more data-insights are retained

Description: Ask whether the user is satisfied with raw data and switch filter options and would like to proceed
If 24-h cropping is selected yet user-defined crop parameters would not retain 24-h recordings, the user is re-directed to provide alternative specifications
This operates identically to reset24, yet through an alternative logic loop
Confirms that the user is satisfied with crop specifications
Ensures that band-pass filter operation can occur (i.e., measureSpan < setTime)
Confirms that the user is satisfied with mass filtering specifications
Confirms that the user is satisfied with a chip filter
If the user is not satisfied with a visualised chip filter, present specifications can either be adjusted or removed to progress with other filters
Confirms that the user is satisfied with all applied chip filters
Confirms that the user is satisfied with calculated derivatives
Confirms that the user is satisfied with light filtering
Confirms that the user is satisfied with all data filtering
Confirms that the user is satisfied with data alignment and final cropping
